It parses the printed path, then asserts the parent is dest and the name fully matches cottonwood-\d{8}T\d{6}Z(-\d+)?\.db. It opens the copy and asserts user_version 2 and the suppression email. The test file passed (13/13).

test_backup_to_missing_folder_exits_1_and_creates_nothing runs main(['backup','--db',src,'--to',missing]) with a nonexistent folder. It asserts code == EXIT_REFUSED, which is 1 (cottonwood/cli.py:17). It asserts the captured stderr contains 'backup folder does not exist: <missing path>'. It asserts the missing folder does not exist afterwards, and that the tmp_path listing is identical to the listing taken before the call, so nothing was created. The test passed when run (1 passed).

results.evidence: test_backup_of_missing_database_exits_1_and_names_it runs main(['backup','--db',<nonexistent>,'--to',dest]) and asserts the return code equals EXIT_REFUSED, which is 1 (cottonwood/cli.py:17). It also asserts that stderr contains 'database does not exist: <path>', so the path is named. The test passed when I ran it (1 passed). The message text comes from cottonwood/backup.py:29.
results.quote:
def test_backup_of_missing_database_exits_1_and_names_it(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    dest = tmp_path / "backups"
    dest.mkdir()
    missing = tmp_path / "absent.db"

    code = main(["backup", "--db", str(missing), "--to", str(dest)])

    assert code == EXIT_REFUSED
    assert f"database does not exist: {missing}" in capsys.readouterr().err

results.evidence: Three parts hold. (1) .env.example is not ignored: `git check-ignore -v .env.example` exits 1 and prints no match. It is currently untracked, not ignored. I could not run `git add` or `git ls-files` here because the work is uncommitted and I am read-only. Since nothing ignores it, `sir task finish --commit` staging all changes will track it, so I judge 'tracked' assessable as 'trackable, and will be committed'. (2) `git check-ignore -v data/backups/x.db` succeeds and reports `.gitignore:19:data/`. For `.env`, I could not run the command because the hook blocks it. .gitignore line 25 is the bare pattern `.env`, with the comment 'Local secrets and overrides; the committed template is .env.example'. A slash-free pattern matches any file named exactly `.env`, and it does not match `.env.example`. So `git check-ignore .env` will succeed. Nothing in the file negates it, and `.env` was not run directly. (3) `grep -riEn 'smtp|sendgrid|mailgun|api_key|password' .env.example config/` returns no matches. .env.example holds only comments and two commented-out path variables (COTTONWOOD_DB and COTTONWOOD_CONFIG). config/pilot.yaml holds only `paths.backup_dir: data/backups`. There are no credential values.

_claim_name in cottonwood/backup.py creates files exclusively. On FileExistsError it increments the suffix, so the second name is cottonwood-<stamp>-2.db. tests/test_backup.py::test_two_backups_in_the_same_second_get_distinct_names freezes the clock and takes three backups. It asserts the names are ...Z.db, ...Z-2.db and ...Z-3.db, that the directory holds exactly those three files, and that each is a valid copy. I ran the test with -k same_second and it passed (1 passed).
